mechanism_narrative: The significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w, following a sharp dip, signals a renewed return to office and commuting routines. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES mobility showing a sustained recovery above -20% for the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated above 7% for two consecutive weeks, it indicates a persistent preference for home-based activities and reduced discretionary outings. This sustained behavior will suppress retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 points over the next 14 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 7% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and strong rebound in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w, recovering from their t-1w lows, suggests a significant easing of mobility restrictions or a strong return-to-office push. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing a sustained increase of more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: In a generally low mobility environment, a sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility, such as the 22.3-point decline observed at t-0w, indicates a widespread reluctance for outdoor activities. candidate_trigger: PARKS drops by more than 20 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 points in the week following a week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility exceeding 20 points.

This sustained pattern will continue to suppress overall retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a sustained increase of more than 5 points over the next 28 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining consistently below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: If RETAIL_REC mobility itself shows a week-on-week increase of more than 4 points, it signals a positive momentum shift in consumer confidence and willingness to engage in discretionary activities. candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines by more than 2 points in the two weeks following a week-on-week increase of more than 4 points.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility experiences a sharp decline (e.g., t-0w) while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated, it suggests a collective preference for indoor home-based leisure over both outdoor and commercial activities. candidate_trigger: PARKS drops by > 20 points week-on-week AND RESIDENTIAL > 7%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 points in the week following a sharp PARKS drop combined with RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 7%.
